name: THE COMPANY VAULT
materialIdentity: The Improvement Company's iron vault behind Fanshawe's office: the great round door, the real ledgers, the deeds of the whole town, the search fund, the private map, the strongbox, the champagne for the day; lit by an oil lamp on the floor under a gas lamp never lit (errata 99 I)
note: Room 35, doc 20: the Company vault, off Fanshawe's office (11), gated to Act IV. Sixteen subjects (doc 54), nobody, no puzzle. In through THE SAFE in Room 11 from Act IV; out by THE VAULT DOOR (errata 99 I).

exits.name: THE VAULT DOOR

LOOK_AT.say: A door from a city bank, freighted here whole. It cost more than everything it protects, which the Colonel would call an investment in impressions.
repeat: The bolts are as thick as my wrist, and there are eleven of them. Somebody counted his secrets and ordered a bolt for each.
It stands open. For a door this expensive, it looks very tired of the arrangement.

LISTEN_TO.say: The mechanism, oiled and huge. It breathes better than most residents.
repeat: The tumblers ticking faintly as the door settles on its hinges.
A long iron sigh when I lean on it. The most honest thing in the building is the weight of this door.

exits.note: Doc 54: the great door, standing open -- the way back into Fanshawe's office (doc 20).

generated.note: GENERATED. Edit the documents or the annotation, never this file.

entrances.note: In through the great door, at left.

LOOK_AT.say: Two hundred claims, unsold, held quietly. All of them adjoining Claim One. Every piece of ground a man might dig near the strike belongs to the Company, and has for years.
repeat: Every one is drawn properly, right side up, with a boundary description. They kept the good paperwork for themselves.
Two hundred claims, and one gap in the ring around Claim One. The gap is mine.
Nothing. Two hundred claims nobody is allowed to dig, keeping very quiet about it.
The bundle shifting as I set it down. Paper, heavier than any of it is worth.

LOOK_AT.say: Shares in the Consolation Improvement Company, beautifully engraved, with a sunrise over a gold field that does not exist.
repeat: These are unsigned. The Company kept its own shares and sold the town everything else.
Each one has a vignette of a miner holding up a nugget and smiling. He has the same face as Obadiah Mott.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Engraved paper is very confident and very quiet.
repeat: A stack shifting, crisp, like cards being squared.
Nothing. The sunrise on them has been rising for twelve years without a sound.

LOOK_AT.say: One bottle, dusty, laid down with a label in Fanshawe's hand: FOR THE DAY.
repeat: The dust on it is twelve years thick. I wrote nothing in it, which took some restraint.
FOR THE DAY. I begin to think he meant the day he'd no longer need to lie, and that he never once expected it to come.
then: He's never said which day. I begin to suspect the bottle is the point.

repeat: A tiny tick from the cork as the vault cools. Hope, pressing.
Nothing. It has waited this long. It can wait for somebody else's day.

overrides.OPEN: FOR THE DAY, says the label. It isn't my day to declare. Though it is closer than the Colonel thinks.

LOOK_AT.say: A fixed lamp, plumbed for gas that does not exist within a thousand miles.
repeat: The mantle has never been lit. It's as white as the day it was unpacked.
There is an oil lamp on the floor beneath it, doing all the work.
then: Installed for how it looks unlit. The whole Company, in one fitting.

LISTEN_TO.say: A hollow pipe. It hums when the vault door moves, an organ note for an empty church.
repeat: The hum again, when the door moves.
Nothing. It's very good at being unlit.

overrides.USE: Plumbed for gas that does not exist within a thousand miles. I turned the key. Nothing, magnificently.

LOOK_AT.say: The subscription book for the Mott Search Fund, twelve years of donations from three territories. The search is the Company's best property and it is very well maintained.
repeat: The donations get smaller every year and more numerous. The search is kept alive by the people who can least afford it.
The last entry is from Ohio, two dollars, with a note: FOR THE FINDING. It was entered in the same hand as all the others.

LISTEN_TO.say: Banknotes settle differently than paper. Softer. Better fed.
repeat: Nothing. A book of other people's hope, closed.
The binding creaks as it opens. It is used to being opened by someone more interested in the totals.

LOOK_AT.say: The actual money, in the actual box. Less than the town believes.
repeat: Coin, sorted by denomination, and a great deal of air between the stacks.
I'd expected to want it. I find I don't.
then: The Company's fortune is mostly the town's belief, held at interest.

LISTEN_TO.say: Coin, but thinly. An echo with good posture.
repeat: A coin turning over as I set the lid down. A small, embarrassed sound.
Nothing. Less money than the door suggests, and it knows it.

overrides.PICK_UP: Lighter than its reputation, which is the Company entire. I put it down before the metaphor could finish.

LOOK_AT.say: A drawer with its own lock, its own key, and its own smell of good tobacco.
repeat: The key isn't here. The Colonel carries it, I imagine, next to the five versions of his war.
It's the one locked thing in the vault. Everything else he has kept for the Company. This he has kept for himself.
then: Whatever the Colonel keeps from the Company, he keeps here.

LISTEN_TO.say: One paper, sliding when the drawer is tried. A single secret, loosely filed.
repeat: The paper inside sliding again, alone.
Nothing. Whatever is in there, he has kept it quiet longer than the gold.

overrides.PULL: Locked, and the lock is better than the vault's. Whatever the Colonel keeps from the Company matters more to him than the money he keeps for it.

LOOK_AT.say: The subscription for the Mott expedition, Boston, 1846. Eleven names. The fourth is A.
repeat: Eleven names, all signed in the same confident ink. Ten of them, I would guess, never saw this territory.
Fanshawe's signature is the smallest on the page. It is the only modest thing he has ever done, and it was the start of everything.
then: Fanshawe. He was not a colonel then either.

repeat: Nothing. Paper twelve years old, keeping the oldest secret in town.
The page lifting a little in the draft from the door, then lying back down.

LOOK_AT.say: Four gross of portraits of a man in a good collar, purchased at wholesale in 1851. The Clarion has been printing him as Obadiah Mott for seven years.
repeat: Four gross, less however many the Clarion has used. The boxes are still nearly full. There is a great deal of Obadiah Mott left.
He has a kind face, the man in the collar. I hope he never learned what became of it.
Card, packed tight, the way you pack anything bought by the gross.
Nothing. A great many copies of one man, and not one of them has anything to say.

LOOK_AT.say: The originals of all eleven maps to Mott's strike. Same hand. Same paper. Same ink.
repeat: On every map the strike is somewhere else. On every map it is marked with exactly the same little cross.
There is a twelfth map, half drawn, the ink still bright. The Colonel was planning another edition.
then: They were drawn in an afternoon.

repeat: Paper rustling as I lift one. Lighter than it should be, for what it cost the town.
Nothing. Eleven maps to nowhere, in perfect agreement.

LOOK_AT.say: Letters to Boston. Nine years of them, copied out in his own hand, all saying the same thing in different words: that the search continues, that hopes are high, and that further funds would be timely.
repeat: Each letter is warmer than the last. By the ninth year he writes to Boston like a man writing home.
The replies aren't in the file. Either Boston stopped answering or he stopped keeping what it said.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. A file of copies keeps its originals to itself.
repeat: Paper sliding inside the folder when I tilt it.
Nothing. Nine years of the same letter, and not one of them said aloud.

LOOK_AT.say: Tin boxes of deeds, labeled by street. The Company owns the fronts, the backs, the lots between, and the mortgage on most of what it doesn't. Consolation, in a filing system.
repeat: My hotel is in here. So is the Nugget, and the church roof, and the ground under the Clarion.
The box marked MAIN STREET is the heaviest. The town's spine, in tin.

LISTEN_TO.say: Tin, ticking with the temperature. The town, expanding and contracting.
repeat: A lid shifting as the vault cools.
Nothing. Property keeps very still when it is being looked at.

LOOK_AT.say: Another map of the district — but this one has the Company's true holdings, and pins where the search is to be steered next. Away, always, from anything owned. It is a map of where gold must never be found.
repeat: Year by year the pins move outward. The search has been walking politely away from Claim One for twelve years.
It is beautifully drawn. It would be the best map in the territory, if it were trying to help anyone.

LISTEN_TO.say: Pins in cork. The quietest rigging imaginable.
repeat: A pin dropping out of the cork and ticking on the floor.
Nothing. The rigging has done its work.

overrides.USE: A map of where gold must never be found. I checked one spot. My claim is not marked. Nobody ever thought to steer anyone away from Prosperity. Nobody ever had to.

LOOK_AT.say: One chair, inside a vault, facing the boxes. Someone sits in here, with the money and the maps, and thinks. The upholstery says: often, and at length.
repeat: It faces the strongbox, not the maps. Whoever sits here sits looking at what he has, not at what he says.
On the floor beside it, a glass with a finger of whisky in it, untouched. He pours, even here, and doesn't drink.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. What gets thought in here doesn't leak.
repeat: Leather settling. It was sat in today.
Nothing. The thinking done in this chair has never been said aloud anywhere.

LOOK_AT.say: The Company's books, bound in green, immaculate.
repeat: The Company's actual accounts. It has never once traded in gold. It trades in maps, permits, tools, filings, lots, lumber and hope, and it has been extraordinarily profitable.
The last page of the last book is ruled off neatly. Somebody knew this year might be the last and wanted the totals tidy.
then: Every year of the search, entered twice: once as it happened, once as it pays.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Double entries keep each other quiet.
repeat: Nothing.
The shelf creaks under twelve years of very profitable nothing.

lamps.note: The oil lamp on the floor, the only light: a slow flame (invariant 9).

figureLight.note: Errata 109, from the pre-playthrough art audit: Thad is drawn in even light so he can go in every room, and here, where the room around him averages 20.6 (of 255) against his 57, he read as pasted on. Graded to about 46, the room's surround plus 25 -- the margin the lit rooms keep -- under a warm lamp multiply gentle enough to keep his coat blue, as the Nugget's (variant B, Tyler, 2026-11-01).
